costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an N18B16A typically takes 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes. A professional engine rebuild can consume 20-30 hours of labour time.
paragraphs: (A used N18B16A engine is available from approximately £1,695 supply-only. All other figures . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

What moves the price for the N18B16A is whether the timing chain, guides and tensioner have been replaced (the primary failure on these engines), whether the high-pressure fuel pump has been addressed, and whether the engine comes complete with ancillaries (turbo, injectors, HPFP) or as a bare long block. A used engine with documented timing chain and HPFP history commands a premium; a bare block with ancillaries removed is cheaper. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: MINI N18B16A Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing chain guide wear and tensioner failure - all years
items.whatHappens: The N18B16A's timing chain guides are made from plastic that becomes brittle over time. As the tensioner spring weakens, the chain can slacken, causing a characteristic ticking or rattling noise at idle. If the chain skips, pistons can contact valves, causing catastrophic internal engine damage. The N18 is more reliable than the earlier N14 in this respect, but timing chain issues remain the primary failure point.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early - when the rattle first appears - replacing the timing chain kit (chain, guides, tensioner) is the cost-effective fix. Chain replacement typically costs £800-£1,500 at an independent specialist. If ignored and the chain jumps, the engine will typically need a full replacement or rebuild.

items.title: High-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure - pre-2012 models
items.whatHappens: The direct injection high-pressure fuel pump is a known weak point on the N18. Symptoms include rough running, hard starting, loss of power, and misfire codes. In mid-2012, N18 engines were fitted with Bosch HPFPs, which are not interchangeable with the earlier Continental units.
items.repairVsReplace: The HPFP must be replaced as a unit - not serviceable. Replacement costs £500-£900, including labour. Always verify which pump type your engine requires before purchasing.

items.title: VANOS solenoid and Valvetronic failure - all years
items.whatHappens: The variable valve timing (VANOS) solenoids and Valvetronic system can fail, leading to rough idling, hesitation on acceleration, reduced power, and engine management lights. Carbon deposits on intake valves (direct injection coking) also contribute to poor running.
items.repairVsReplace: VANOS solenoid cleaning or replacement typically costs £300-£600. Valvetronic motor or eccentric shaft issues can be more significant - £600-£1,200. Carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) costs £400-£700.

items.title: Oil consumption - higher-mileage units
items.whatHappens: Many N18 engines develop oil consumption issues as they age, often due to worn piston rings or valve stem seals. This is a known complaint on specialised forums.
items.repairVsReplace: If consumption is mild (1L per 1,000 miles), regular top-ups may be tolerable. Severe consumption (1L per 500 miles or less) typically requires engine strip-down - often uneconomical versus fitting a replacement unit.

failures.goodYearsLine: The N18B16A is considered significantly more reliable than its predecessor, the N14. Post-2012 engines received revised HPFP components and timing chain tensioner updates that have reduced failure rates .

variants.title: N18B16A - One Engine, Multiple Tunes
variants.intro: The N18B16A is a specific engine code within BMW's Prince engine family, but it spans multiple power outputs and vehicle applications. The core hardware - 1.6-litre aluminium block, 77mm bore × 85.8mm stroke, 10.5:1 compression ratio - is consistent across all variants; tuning and ancillaries differentiate them. Fitted to: MINI Cooper S (R56/R55/R57/R58/R59/R60) - all body styles Key technical difference: 135 kW (184 PS), 240 Nm torque. This is the most common N18B16A variant fitted to UK MINIs. Features a BorgWarner K03 turbocharger. Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above (timing chain guide wear, HPFP issues on pre-2012, VANOS/Valvetronic failures, oil consumption). Interchange note: Direct swap with other N18B16A Cooper S variants of the same year. Note that pre- and post-2012 HPFP units are not interchangeable. Fitted to: MINI John Cooper Works (R56/R55/R57), MINI Cooper S JCW (R58/R59/R60) Key technical difference: 140 kW (190 PS), 260 Nm torque. Same block and head, different ECU calibration and potentially different turbocharger specification. Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family pattern; higher boost and power output may accelerate timing chain and turbocharger wear. Interchange note: A Cooper S can accept a JCW-spec N18B16A with the correct ECU remap, but ancillaries (injectors, turbocharger) may differ. Fitted to: Some MINI One variants (non-UK markets), BMW 116i (E87), BMW 316i (E90) Key technical difference: Lower 90 kW (122 PS) output. Same hardware, different ECU calibration. Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family pattern; lower power output means marginally less stress on timing components and turbocharger.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement N18B16A - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used N18B16A makes sense for lower-value R56 or R55 MINIs where a reconditioned unit would exceed the car's value. However, the timing chain and HPFP are the critical risks - only buy a used unit with documented chain history and HPFP service records, or from a car that was running well at removal. Mileage under 60,000 is preferable. A used bare engine can be found from approximately £1,695.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the sweet spot for most N18B16A replacements. A proper reconditioned unit will have the timing chain, guides and tensioner replaced (addressing the primary failure), a new or tested HPFP, new VANOS solenoids, new piston rings (addressing oil consumption), and a carbon-cleaned cylinder head. Expect 12-24 months warranty and a price of £1,800-£2,800.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is necessary if the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure (valve-piston contact) or severe oil consumption that has damaged cylinder bores. A rebuilt engine should include new pistons, rings, bearings, timing components, a rebuilt cylinder head, and new HPFP. Expect £2,800-£4,200 supply-only.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: EnginesMarket connects you with vetted UK MINI specialists who can supply and fit your N18B16A - nationwide delivery and a minimum 12-month warranty on all reconditioned units.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The N18B16A sits in R-series MINIs typically valued between £2,500 (early Cooper S high-mileage) and £12,000 (JCW / low-mileage examples). If your MINI is worth less than £4,000, a reconditioned unit at £1,800-£2,800 represents 45-70% of the car's value - carefully evaluate whether replacement makes financial sense. For lower-value examples, a good used engine with documented history may be the better economic choice. If the car is worth under £3,000, evaluate scrap value before committing to a reconditioned engine.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the N18B16A engine?
items.answer: Timing chain guide wear and tensioner failure is the primary concern, typically appearing between 60,000-100,000 miles. A ticking or rattling noise at idle is the earliest warning. If caught early, a chain kit replacement (£800-£1,500) prevents catastrophic failure; if ignored, the chain can jump and destroy the engine. High-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure on pre-2012 models (£500-£900 replacement) is also common. VANOS solenoid and Valvetronic issues cause rough idling and hesitation (£300-£600). Oil consumption on higher-mileage units (80,000+ miles) is also common.

items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the front-left side of the block (near the timing chain cover) and also appears on your V5C logbook under the engine number. If you're unsure, enter your registration on this page and we'll match it to the correct engine code. N18B16A is the 1.6-litre turbo petrol (184-190 hp) - used in MINI Cooper S/JCW and some BMW models. N14B16A is the earlier 1.6-litre turbo petrol (2006-2010) - higher failure rate. N16B16A is the naturally aspirated 1.6-litre petrol (122 hp) - used in MINI Cooper/One. B48A20A is the 2.0-litre turbo petrol that replaced the N18 from 2014.

items.question: Is the N18B16A a reliable engine overall?
items.answer: The N18B16A is considered significantly more reliable than its predecessor, the N14 - but it is not without its weaknesses. With proper maintenance - including 5W-30 LL-01 oil, regular coolant checks, 10,000-mile service intervals, and prompt attention to any rattling noises - the N18 can be a dependable engine. The timing chain guides remain the primary weak point, but the N18 is less prone to catastrophic failure than the N14. Pre-2012 HPFP failures are common - ensure this has been addressed on any used purchase. Regular oil changes with BMW-approved oil are essential to prevent timing chain and carbon buildup issues. 2012-onwards engines have revised HPFP and timing chain tensioner components that have improved reliability.
